newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan urges quick resumption of Israel-Syria talks.
newsitem.headline: Annan urges quick resumption of Israel-Syria talks.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan urged on Wednesday the speedy resumption of stalled peace talks between Israel and Syria and Lebanon.

Speaking at the opening of the 1997 session of the U.N. committee on the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, he said "courageous new steps" had been taken in the Middle East in the past few years.

The peace process gained important momentum only last month as a result of an agreement between Israel and the Palestinians on Hebron and other issues, Annan said, addressing the committee for the first time since he took office on Jan. 1.

"At times there have been setbacks. But, by and large, the vision inherent in the Declaration of Principles has been sustained," Annan said, referring to the basic accord signed by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993.

"It is now of the utmost importance not to dissipate those achievements, but to build on them in order to fulfil the hopes of all the peoples of the region. For the Middle East peace process to flourish, progress is also required in the Israeli-Syrian and Israeli-Lebanese tracks," he said.
"This will be crucial for the realisation of a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement... It is my earnest hope that these negotiations will resume quickly," he added.
Promoting economic and social development was essential to improve living conditions, especially in Gaza, and to create solid foundations for peace, he said.
The United Nations was making an important contribution, with special emphasis on generating employment and Palestinian institution-building.

"But we can do more," the secretary-general said, noting his recent appointment of Chinmaya Gharekhan, a former Indian career diplomat and senior U.N. official, as the U.N. special coordinator in the occupied territories.
"In the weeks ahead he will work closely with the Palestinian Authority to identify areas in which the U.N. can enhance its contribution in the economic and social fields," Annan said.
